The catalogue provides broad coverage of the ethical concerns identified in the study. Although some overlap exists between certain clusters, this does not significantly reduce the overall coverage.

The recurring structure is coherent because it moves from understanding the concern to implementing safeguards, communicating relevant information, assessing risks, verifying effectiveness, and responding to issues.

The catalogue provides a useful bridge between high-level ethical concerns and practical software/system engineering activities by linking concerns to actions, possible evidence, SDLC phases, and responsible roles.

The definition is clear and captures both system-level robustness and data-quality aspects. However, the relationship between “resilience” in this cluster and the separate C-04 Reliability, Dependability & Resilience cluster could be clarified to reduce possible overlap. Since “resilience” appears in both C-04 and C-16, I think the boundary between the two clusters could be made clearer.

The mapping is generally semantically appropriate. The connection to Privacy and Data Governance / Intellectual Property and Transparency and Explainability could be explained more explicitly, particularly which aspects of C-16 motivate these mappings.

The ethics-label cards and characteristics provides a coherent way for organizing the concern clusters. It allows the concern cluster to be associated with multiple relevant ethics-label characteristics rather than restricting it to a single category.

The concerns are generally coherent. The main potential overlap is resilience, which also appears in the C-04 Reliability, Dependability & Resilience cluster, so the distinction between the two uses could be clarified.

The proposed actions provide good coverage of the cluster. It could be useful to include an explicit feedback loop, so that findings from monitoring, verification, or incidents lead to reassessment and, where necessary, corrective actions.
The proposed artifacts are plausible and flexible
The proposed SDLC phases are generally appropriate and cover the lifecycle well.
The proposed roles are reasonable and sufficiently broad. Since the cluster also considers system behaviour under attack, a security role could be considered where relevant.

The definition is clear and appropriate. However, since “communication” also appears in other concern clusters, such as C-08 and C-24, its specific scope within C-17 could be clarified to reduce possible overlap.

The mapping is appropriate, particularly for Transparency and Explainability, Principle of Autonomy, and Responsibility and Accountability. The management of adverse effects characteristics are also relevant where inadequate or misleading explanations may contribute to negative impacts.
The ethics-label framework provides a coherent way to organize C-17 because the concerns can be linked to several relevant ethical dimensions rather than a single category.
The concerns are generally coherent and well grouped. However, the scope of “communication” within C-17 could be clarified to distinguish it from communication-related concerns in other clusters.

The proposed actions provide good coverage of the cluster. It could be useful to make the feedback loop (continuous improvement loop) clearer, so that issues identified through verification or stakeholder feedback lead to improvements in the explanation mechanisms.

The proposed artifacts are plausible and sufficiently flexible. They provide useful evidence. It may also be useful to allow stakeholder feedback or user-testing results as evidence, particularly for assessing whether explanations are understandable and useful to their intended audience.
The proposed SDLC phases are plausible and sufficiently flexible.

The roles are well chosen overall because explainability is not only a technical issue; it also involves user understanding, domain context, communication, and governance. One possible observation is that Engineering appears under Protect but not under Respond, even though correcting or updating explanation mechanisms after issues are identified may require technical changes.
The definition is clear and appropriate

The ethics-label framework provides a coherent way to organize C-18 because compliance and data governance relate to several broader ethical dimensions, including privacy, accountability, transparency, and risk management.
